DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Pneumonia secondary to Chorioamnionitis

Based on the presence of respiratory acidosis, hypoxia, and the characteristic ground-glass opacities with air bronchograms on your chest X-ray, combined with the history of potential chorioamnionitis, the clinical picture strongly points to a bacterial infection of the lungs. The blood culture and Gram stain results will be crucial to identify the specific pathogen and guide antibiotic therapy. Please ensure the baby is placed in a warm environment and breathing support is maintained while we await the microbiology results.
